clue.text: Noisy scene behind City tube station

indicators.note: the noisy-scene word comes after, behind, the city in the answer

parts.note: Oxford is the university city
a circus is a scene of noisy chaos

explanation.surface: A commuter complains of the din behind the City of London near a station.
explanation.walkthrough: OXFORD CIRCUS is a busy London Underground station on Oxford Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford Circus is one of the busiest stations on the London Underground, the tube.

clue.text: Scrap books theologian and bishops, say, are found in

indicators.note: these pieces are found inside the books abbreviation

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian
bishops are chess pieces, chessmen

explanation.surface: A scrap of paper lists books by a theologian and some bishops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bishops, say' means chessmen in general, giving MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a scrap or leftover piece, an odd bit of something.

clue.text: Fawn suit, looking good

definitions.meaning: to fawn is to praise someone insincerely, to toady
clothes that suit you make you look good

explanation.surface: A light brown outfit looks smart on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fawn' poses as a colour of suit but is the verb, to toady.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatter is to fawn over someone, and a garment flatters when it suits the wearer.

clue.text: Town's favourite given special treatment

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town in North Yorkshire
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A local hero is fêted by the townsfolk.
explanation.walkthrough: REDCAR is a seaside town in North Yorkshire; 'given' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the red carpet means being given lavish ceremonial welcome.

clue.text: Be punished, having dropped a glass of sherry

indicators.note: dropping a letter means taking it out of the word

parts.note: a copita is a tulip-shaped sherry glass

explanation.surface: Someone gets in trouble for dropping a sherry glass.
explanation.walkthrough: COPITA is a Spanish sherry glass; drop its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Cop it is British slang meaning to get into trouble or be punished.

clue.text: Unruly fellow at bottom of list took part in revolution

indicators.note: in a down answer the unruly fellow sits at the bottom, below the list

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties
a Ted, Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth with a rebellious image

explanation.surface: A rowdy man last on the roster joined an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: A TED, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth known for rowdiness. 'revolution' means turning, not uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rotated took part in a revolution, a turn about an axis.

clue.text: Madden one Parisian on mount

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: un is French for one
a hinge is a small mount for stamps in an album

explanation.surface: A Frenchman on horseback drives someone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: A stamp hinge is a small gummed mount.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhinge is to drive someone mad, to madden.

clue.text: Veteran to miss game?

parts.note: a veteran is old
a miss, a young unmarried woman, is a maid

explanation.surface: An old soldier asks whether he should skip a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' looks like a verb but is the noun, a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Maid is a card game in which the loser is left holding the odd queen.

clue.text: Long to be aboard a vessel

indicators.note: being aboard means being placed inside the other piece

parts.note: per means a, as in so much per head
to long is to itch for something

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to sail on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' gives PER, as in 'ten pounds a head' = per head.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitcher is a jug, a vessel for holding and pouring liquid.

clue.text: Piano virtuoso playing harmonica note very loudly

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are performed in a new order

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud

explanation.surface: A great pianist plays the mouth organ very loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges HARMONICA plus N.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Rachmaninoff was a Russian composer famed as a virtuoso pianist.

clue.text: She sought vengeance, employing chosen gunmen

parts.note: elect means chosen, as in the president-elect
RA, the Royal Artillery, are the army's gunners

explanation.surface: A woman out for revenge hires hand-picked hitmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employing' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra, in Greek myth, urged her brother to avenge their father Agamemnon's murder.

clue.text: Film all about Conservative, elected, working hard

indicators.note: all of the following pieces are turned about, read backwards together

parts.note: a party elected is in
at it means busily working

explanation.surface: A movie praises a Conservative who has won office and is hard at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all about' reverses the whole run CINATIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic is the 1997 blockbuster movie about the sinking liner.

clue.text: Nonsense about union backing teacher

indicators.note: the union piece stands behind, supporting, the turned nonsense

parts.note: TU is short for trade union

indicators.note: about means the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: rot is nonsense

explanation.surface: Rubbish is talked about the union supporting a schoolmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ROT into TOR; 'backing' places TU as the support behind it, at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher or one who instructs a small group.

clue.text: Revolutionary aim appeared, after leaders left, an impossible plan

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests overturning, so the letters are turned into a new order
the first letters, the leaders, of both words leave

explanation.surface: A rebel's goal seemed, once its leaders had gone, a hopeless scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first letters of 'aim' and 'appeared' leaves IM + PPEARED; 'Revolutionary' rearranges those.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe dream is a fanciful hope or plan that will never come true.

clue.text: She bit lip badly, causing inflammation

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: A woman bites her lip hard and it swells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges SHE BIT LIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlebitis is inflammation of the walls of a vein.

clue.text: Storytelling can lead to trouble

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so these letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A warning that telling tales can lead to trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' looks like the end of the warning but is the anagram signal for CAN LEAD TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal means consisting of anecdotes, short stories told about events.

clue.text: Stare at pupil found here

definitions.meaning: the pupil is the dark centre of the eye's globe

explanation.surface: Someone stares at a schoolchild found here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' looks like a schoolchild but is the opening of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball is to look hard at, and the pupil is part of the eye's globe.

clue.text: Boxer with cut beginning to get clearly visible shiner

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a start is a beginning

explanation.surface: A fighter with a cut gets a clearly visible black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' is the breed of dog, and 'shiner' is not a black eye but something that shines: Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dog Star, Sirius, is the brightest star seen from Earth.

clue.text: Record-player used by bar serving spirits

parts.note: a DJ, a disc jockey, plays records
an inn is a pub or bar

explanation.surface: A pub hires a disc jockey while it serves drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' looks like drinks served at the bar, but means genies.
explanation.definitionFit: Djinn are spirits of Arabian and Islamic folklore, genies.

clue.text: Really fed up with move leading to nothing

indicators.note: in a down answer up means the word reads bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to act is to make a move
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone genuinely sick of making moves that come to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FED into DEF.
explanation.definitionFit: De facto means in fact, really, as opposed to in law.

clue.text: Mineral that's covering gold man comes upon

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round the other pieces

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is

indicators.note: in a down answer the man sits on top of the gold

parts.note: Ron is a man's name
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A man stumbles on a mineral layer covering gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is the Latin abbreviation id est; in heraldry gold is or, and 'comes upon' sets the man above it in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron ore is rock from which the metal is extracted, a mineral deposit.

clue.text: Actor liked the stage, making comeback, gripping one

indicators.note: gripping means holding the next piece inside
coming back means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: dug is slang for liked, as in 'I dug that band'
a leg is a stage of a journey or race
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A performer, fond of the theatre, returns to it holding a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' reverses both pieces together, then 'gripping' puts the I into the result; 'liked' is the slang 'dug', not 'enjoyed' in any plainer sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Gielgud was a celebrated English stage and film actor.

clue.text: Sad song caused upset, grating on me at the end

indicators.note: in a down answer upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a grid is a grating of bars

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A mournful tune caused distress, grating on the listener at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns GRID into DIRG; 'caused' and 'on' link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song, a lament for the dead.

clue.text: Someone enthusiastic about entertaining old comic

parts.note: a buff is a keen enthusiast, as in a film buff

indicators.note: entertaining means taking in a guest, holding the next piece

parts.note: on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A fan of comedy hosts a veteran comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts O inside ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffoon is a clown, someone who plays the fool for laughs.

clue.text: Best man's wedding present?

parts.note: read as the best man at a wedding, who raises his glass to the couple, and as a gift couples often receive

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what the best man gave the couple.
explanation.walkthrough: The best man proposes the toasts at a reception, and a kitchen gadget for browning bread is a classic wedding gift.
explanation.definitionFit: The best man makes toasts, and a bread-browning kitchen appliance is a common wedding present.

clue.text: Credit unavailable for carpet

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick
a dish that is off is no longer available

explanation.surface: A shop refuses credit on a rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' is the verb, to reprimand, not a floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to scold them, the same as giving them a dressing-down.

clue.text: Betray Nelson at sea here giving persuasive speech?

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Nelson was betrayed at sea, a spot for smooth talking.
explanation.walkthrough: The BLARNEY STONE, at Blarney Castle in Ireland, is said to give whoever kisses it the gift of persuasive talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Kissing the stone at Blarney Castle is said to bestow eloquence, a flattering gift of the gab.
